h1: The 6 Best Rain Barrels of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 rain barrels from 50 to 60 gallons scored on screens, spigots, overflow, stands and linking, including a collapsible option.
summary: The Step2 Lakewood 60 Gallon is the best rain barrel for most homes, with the biggest capacity here, a stainless steel mesh screen and a 3/4 inch brass spigot on an elevated stand. The RTS Newport 50 Gallon is the pick if you need flexible overflow routing. For linking several barrels, choose the RTS 50 Gallon Walnut, and for winter storage the Laspeiraux collapsible folds flat.
intro: Most rain barrels fail at the overflow, not the storage. A downspout fills a 50 gallon barrel from empty in a few minutes during a real storm, and then the water has to go somewhere. If the barrel has no proper overflow, it floods the foundation you were trying to protect. Capacity gets the headline, but overflow decides whether the barrel helps or hurts.

We ranked six barrels on capacity, screen and lid design, spigot material, overflow and linking, and whether the stand lifts the spigot high enough to fill a watering can. Elevated stands and brass spigots moved a barrel up, while plain fittings and missing details moved it down. Every barrel here is in the $25 to $200 range.

products.name: Step2 Lakewood 60 Gallon Rain Barrel With Stand
products.verdict: 60 gallons, a stainless mesh screen and a brass spigot on an elevated stand.
products.description:
The Lakewood holds 60 gallons, the most in this ranking, and measures 46 inches tall by 24 wide by 20 deep. A stainless steel mesh screen filters debris, and a 3/4 inch brass spigot sits on an elevated stand so a watering can slides underneath.

It ranks first because it combines the largest capacity with the right fittings. A 3/4 inch spigot matches a standard garden hose thread, which many plastic spigots do not. The stainless screen resists tearing and keeps mosquitoes out. The trade is size: at 46 inches tall, it needs a flat, firm pad, and it costs more than basic 50 gallon models.

Best for gardeners with a decent downspout and space for a tall barrel. Check the pad is level before filling it.

products.name: RTS Home Accents 50 Gallon Newport Rain Barrel With Stand
products.verdict: A 50 gallon barrel with a removable lid and an overflow nozzle for either side.
products.description:
The Newport holds 50 gallons and ships with a stand, a brass spigot and a removable lid. The overflow nozzle can be installed on either side, which lets you route excess water toward whichever way slopes away from your house.

It ranks second because the flexible overflow solves the most common rain barrel failure, and the removable lid makes cleaning easy. Against the Lakewood, it holds 10 gallons less and does not list a screen material. What it gives you is practical details that are easy to overlook.

Best where the barrel must sit on a particular side of the downspout. Confirm the overflow hose fits your drainage plan before you buy.
products.skipIf: You want the biggest tank for the money.

products.name: RTS Home Accents 50 Gallon Rain Barrel With Brass Spigot Walnut
products.verdict: UV-resistant polyethylene with a built-in, linkable overflow valve, in the $50 to $100 bracket.
products.description:
This RTS 50 gallon barrel is made from UV-resistant polyethylene, with a brass spigot and a built-in overflow valve that can be linked to another barrel. It sells in the $50 to $100 bracket, cheaper than the stand-equipped models above.

It ranks third because the listing includes no stand, so you must supply a stand or blocks to raise it. What it offers is the ability to chain barrels: one fills, overflow runs to the next, and your storage doubles with a single downspout. UV resistance matters because cheap polyethylene turns brittle in sun.

Best for gardeners who want to expand later. Plan a firm base and a way to lift the barrel off the ground.
products.idealFor: Gardeners planning to link two or more barrels.
products.skipIf: You want a stand included in the box.

products.name: RTS Home Accents Premium 55 Gallon Rain Barrel Removable Lid
products.verdict: A 55 gallon flat-back barrel that sits flush against a wall.
products.description:
The Premium holds 55 gallons, has a removable lid, a brass spigot and a flat-back shape that sits flush against a wall or downspout. That flat profile saves several inches of depth compared with a round barrel.

It ranks fourth because the listing does not mention a stand, an overflow arrangement or a screen. Its 55 gallons fall between the Newport and the Lakewood. The flat back is what you pay for: on a narrow side yard, the extra inches matter.

Best for tight spaces along a wall. Check what overflow fittings come with it before you rely on it in a heavy storm.
pros: Flat back sits flush to a wall
products.idealFor: Narrow side yards where depth is limited.
products.skipIf: You need a stand, screen and overflow in the box.

products.name: Good Ideas Impressions Nantucket 50 Gallon Rain Barrel
products.verdict: A 50 gallon barrel with a 4 inch planter top and two metal spigots.
products.description:
The Nantucket holds 50 gallons and has a 4 inch planter top, a mesh screen to block debris and two metal spigots, one at the front and one at the side. The planter top lets you grow flowers on the lid.

It ranks fifth because the planter top is a decoration, not a function, and a second spigot is helpful but not essential. A mesh screen is included, though the material is not stated. Against the Newport, you get two spigots instead of flexible overflow. Water sits near the planter soil, so keep the lid clean.

Best for front yards where a barrel should look like part of the garden. Check the spigot threads suit your hose.
products.idealFor: Visible front-yard spots where looks matter.
products.skipIf: You want a stand or flexible overflow.

products.name: Laspeiraux 53 Gallon Collapsible Rain Barrel PVC
products.verdict: A 53 gallon three-layer PVC barrel that folds away for winter.
products.description:
The Laspeiraux stores 53 gallons in a three-layer PVC body that folds flat for storage, with a screw-in faucet. It sits in the $25 to $50 bracket, the lowest price here.

It ranks last because PVC bladders stretch and bulge when full, a collapsible barrel has no rigid stand, and a screw-in faucet is less robust than brass. The trade is storage: in a cold climate you can fold it away before freezing, which protects hard barrels from cracking. For a renter or a seasonal gardener, that matters.

Best for temporary setups and small gardens. Place it on a flat, protected surface and do not leave it full through a freeze.
products.idealFor: Renters and seasonal gardeners with limited storage.
products.skipIf: You want a permanent, rigid barrel.

whatMatters.detail: A 1,000 square foot roof sheds roughly 600 gallons per inch of rain, so any single barrel fills fast. Capacity of 50 to 60 gallons suits a small garden, and linking two barrels doubles it. Check the listing for capacity, and consider how much rain your downspout actually collects.

Once the barrel is full, extra water must go somewhere safe. A flexible nozzle, like the Newport's, or a linkable valve, like the RTS Walnut's, directs it away from the foundation. Check where the overflow outlet sits, and attach a hose that drains downhill and away.

A fine screen keeps leaves and mosquitoes out, and standing water without one breeds larvae. Stainless steel mesh, as on the Lakewood, outlasts plastic. A removable lid helps cleaning. Look for the screen material in the listing, not just a note that debris is blocked.

A full barrel gives low pressure, and the higher the spigot, the better the flow. Brass spigots outlast plastic, and a 3/4 inch thread fits a hose. A stand lifts the spigot so a watering can fits underneath. Check the listing for stand inclusion and spigot size.

UV-resistant polyethylene resists cracking in sun, while PVC bladders such as the Laspeiraux fold flat but stretch. In freezing climates, drain hard barrels before winter, because expanding ice can split them. Check material and cold-weather advice in the manufacturer's instructions.

faq.q: Can I link two rain barrels together?
faq.a: Yes, if they have a linkable overflow. The RTS 50 Gallon Walnut has a built-in valve for chaining barrels, while the Newport has an overflow nozzle. Link them at the same height and use a short hose.

faq.q: What is the biggest rain barrel mistake?
faq.a: Ignoring the overflow. A 50 gallon barrel fills in minutes, and unmanaged overflow floods the foundation. Use the Newport's side-flexible nozzle or a linkable valve, and always point the hose downhill away from the house.

faq.q: Is the Step2 Lakewood worth it over a cheaper barrel?
faq.a: For long-term use, yes. Its 60 gallons, stainless mesh screen and brass spigot outlast the plastic fittings on cheap barrels. If you only need a few pots watered, the Laspeiraux is cheaper but less durable.

faq.q: How do I set up a barrel on a downspout?
faq.a: Level a firm pad, set the barrel or stand on it, then cut the downspout above the lid and fit a diverter or elbow. Water weighs about 8 pounds per gallon, so a full Lakewood needs solid ground.
Keep the barrel fully covered with a fine screen. The Lakewood uses stainless mesh, and the Nantucket a mesh screen. Check seams regularly, and empty any water that collects in a planter top.

faq.q: Do I need to empty rain barrels in winter?
faq.a: In freezing climates, yes. Ice expands and can crack rigid barrels, so drain and disconnect them. The Laspeiraux collapsible folds flat for storage, which is simpler than draining a 55 gallon hard barrel.

finalTake: The Step2 Lakewood 60 Gallon Rain Barrel With Stand is the best buy for most homes: the most capacity, a stainless screen and a brass spigot on a stand. Pick the RTS Newport when overflow direction matters, and the RTS 50 Gallon Walnut if you plan to link barrels. The Laspeiraux collapsible is the budget answer for seasonal use. Whatever you choose, plan the overflow first.
